We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl which has a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline.

We need 3 reactions: likely (1) sulfonamide formation (attach sulfonyl chloride to aniline). (2) amide formation (couple carboxylic acid to aniline). (3) Doebner modification to create the α,β-unsaturated acid (or maybe the unsaturated amide). Let's think retrosynthetic direction: target -> disconnect amide bond between carbonyl and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). That gives acid precursor: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait the amide carbonyl attached to the trans-alkene: /C=C/C(=O)N-... So cleavage gives acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Actually the acid would be the α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to phenyl-sulfonyl group. So precursor 1: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1 (the acid). Then step 2: that acid could be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl-sulfonyl aldehyde) and malonic acid. So precursor 2: aromatic aldehyde: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(=O)cc2)cc1? Wait the aldehyde is on the phenyl-sulfonyl ring at the position where the unsaturated chain attaches. So the aldehyde is: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1. That's the aldehyde precursor.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: we need sulfonyl chloride and aniline (p-tolyl amine). The sulfonyl chloride derived from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to p-tolyl ring. So we need p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, TsCl) reacting with the aniline (the phenyl ring that later becomes the aldehyde). Wait the sulfonamide is attached to the p-tolyl ring (the left phenyl). The sulfonyl group is attached to the left phenyl via N (i.e., the left phenyl has an NH-SO2-Ph? Actually SMILES: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the left phenyl has a substituent N-SO2-Ph (the right phenyl). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to left phenyl (an aniline) and the sulfonyl group attached to right phenyl. So the sulfonamide formation is between left aniline (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from right phenyl (the sulfonyl chloride of the right phenyl). So step 3: combine p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) with sulfonyl chloride of the right phenyl (which is a phenyl sulfonyl chloride bearing the aldehyde substituent). So we need to generate that sulfonyl chloride precursor: the right phenyl with sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl) attached to it, plus the aldehyde substituent. So precursor 3: aromatic sulfonyl chloride: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1? Wait the right phenyl also has the aldehyde substituent. So the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl that also has the aldehyde at para position? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the right phenyl at position 1 (connected to N). The aldehyde is at para to that? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2. The aldehyde is not on that phenyl; the aldehyde is part of the side chain attached to that phenyl. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is just the phenyl sulfonyl chloride (no aldehyde). Then after sulfonamide formation, we have the phenyl-sulfonamide attached to left phenyl. Then later we need to install the side chain (aldehyde then Doebner). Actually the side chain is attached to the right phenyl (the one bearing sulfonyl). So after sulfonamide formation, we have the right phenyl with sulfonamide attached, and we need to add the side chain via Doebner on that phenyl. So order: 1) sulfonamide formation (connect left aniline with sulfonyl chloride of right phenyl). 2) Doebner modification on right phenyl to install α,β-unsaturated acid side chain (starting from aldehyde). 3) amide coupling with aniline (the aniline is the third phenyl attached to amide). Wait the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). That's a separate aniline (third phenyl). So after we have the unsaturated acid attached to right phenyl, we couple with aniline (aniline) to form amide.

Thus three steps: (i) sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and phenyl sulfonyl chloride (giving sulfonamide). (ii) Doebner modification on the phenyl (with aldehyde) to give α,β-unsaturated acid. (iii) amide coupling with aniline to give final product.
